about.title: À propos d'Instant Typing
privacy.s1_body: Instant Typing (instanttyping.com) est construit sur une architecture axée sur la confidentialité. Nous croyons que votre vitesse de frappe et vos schémas de frappe sont des données personnelles. Contrairement aux plateformes de frappe traditionnelles qui enregistrent les frappes sur des serveurs externes ou nécessitent la création obligatoire d'un compte, notre moteur de test principal s'exécute entièrement dans le runtime de votre navigateur local.
terms.s6_body: Nous nous réservons le droit de réviser ou de remplacer ces conditions à tout moment. L'utilisation continue de la plateforme après la publication des mises à jour constitue l'acceptation contraignante des conditions modifiées.

Étant donné que nous ne maintenons pas de comptes ni ne stockons d'enregistrements identifiables sur des bases de données distantes, la suppression de votre stockage local du navigateur supprime complètement toutes les traces de votre activité.

faq.idx.title: Foire aux questions sur les tests de frappe
faq.idx.q1: Comment les mots par minute (MPM) sont-ils calculés sur Instant Typing ?
faq.idx.a1: Suivant les directives internationales standard de mesure de la frappe, un mot est défini comme exactement cinq frappes. Le MPM net est calculé comme : (Frappes correctes / 5) divisé par le temps écoulé en minutes.
faq.idx.q2: Quelle est la vitesse de frappe moyenne ?
faq.idx.a2: La vitesse de frappe moyenne mondiale est d'environ 40 MPM. Les professionnels tapent généralement entre 65 et 85 MPM, tandis que les dactylographes de compétition atteignent plus de 100 à 120 MPM.
faq.idx.q3: Quelle est la différence entre le MPM brut et le MPM net ?
faq.idx.a3: Le MPM brut représente le nombre total de frappes divisé par 5 par minute, qu'elles soient correctes ou non. Le MPM net ne compte que les caractères correctement tapés.
faq.idx.q4: Comment fonctionne la fonctionnalité 'Entraîner mes erreurs' ?
faq.idx.a4: Lorsque vous terminez un test avec des erreurs, notre moteur isole les mots qui ont déclenché des fautes de frappe et génère un exercice ciblé.
faq.idx.q5: Puis-je télécharger un certificat de dactylographie ?
faq.idx.a5: Oui. Après avoir terminé un test, cliquez sur 'Voir le certificat de compétence'. Vous pouvez télécharger ce certificat pour vos CV ou portfolios.
faq.1.title: Frequently Asked Questions About the 1-Minute Test
faq.1.q1: Why is the 1-minute typing test the standard benchmark?
faq.1.a1: A 60-second test provides the optimal balance between measuring peak burst speed and sustaining consistent finger rhythm without causing hand strain. Most recruitment portals and standardized assessments utilize 1-minute intervals to evaluate core keyboard proficiency.
faq.1.q2: How can I quickly increase my 1-minute WPM score?
faq.1.a2: Focus on zero-error bursts. Slow down slightly on long words to avoid backspacing. Sit with elbows bent at 90 degrees, keep wrists elevated off the desk, and anchor your index fingers on the F and J keys before beginning.
faq.1.q3: How often should I practice the 60-second typing test?
faq.1.a3: Three to five 1-minute sessions daily produce far better retention than a single exhausting marathon session. Consistent daily repetition allows your motor cortex to consolidate finger muscle memory.
faq.3.title: Frequently Asked Questions About Extended Typing Tests
faq.3.q1: Why do employers use 3-minute and 5-minute typing tests?
faq.3.a1: While 1-minute tests measure maximum burst speed, employment tests require stamina and consistent rhythm over extended periods. Civil service examinations, legal secretarial positions, and data entry assessments use 3-to-5 minute tests to verify that typists maintain high accuracy without succumbing to fatigue.
faq.3.q2: What is an acceptable WPM score for a 3-minute employment test?
faq.3.a2: Most government and clerical jobs require a sustained Net WPM of 45 to 60 with a minimum accuracy rate of 95% to 98%. Specialized positions like medical transcriptionists or stenographers often require 70 to 90+ sustained WPM.
faq.3.q3: How do I prevent wrist fatigue during longer typing assessments?
faq.3.a3: Ensure your wrists remain neutral and hovered above the desk surface rather than resting on the hard table edge. Adjust your chair height so that your forearms are parallel to the floor, and take brief micro-pauses between sentences to relax your finger tension.
faq.typing.title: Frequently Asked Questions for Beginners
faq.typing.q1: What is touch typing and why is it essential?
faq.typing.a1: Touch typing is typing solely through tactile muscle memory without looking down at the physical keyboard. By anchoring your fingers on the home row (ASDF JKL;), your brain maps the location of every key relative to your home position, allowing your typing speed to triple or quadruple compared to hunt-and-peck typing.
faq.typing.q2: What are the tactile bumps on the F and J keys for?
faq.typing.a2: The small raised ridges on the 'F' and 'J' keys are tactile indicators designed to help you locate the home row without glancing down. Your left index finger rests on 'F' and your right index finger rests on 'J'.
faq.typing.q3: Is 20 WPM good for a complete beginner?
faq.typing.a3: Yes! When transitioning to true touch typing, speeds initially drop as your fingers learn new geometric pathways. Reaching 20 to 25 WPM with correct finger placement is an excellent initial milestone. Within two weeks of daily 10-minute practice, speeds typically jump to 40+ WPM.
faq.numbers.title: Frequently Asked Questions About Number & Symbol Typing
faq.numbers.q1: Why is typing numbers and punctuation so much harder than plain words?
faq.numbers.a1: Most typists practice only lowercase alphabetic words. The number row (1-0) requires stretching fingers upward beyond the top row, while symbols require coordinating the Shift key with the opposite hand. Without dedicated practice, typists look down at their hands for numbers, immediately slowing to a halt.
faq.numbers.q2: Should I use the top number row or the 10-key numeric keypad?
faq.numbers.a2: For typing text interspersed with numbers (such as coding, legal documents, or alphanumeric addresses), mastering the top number row via touch typing is essential because moving your right hand back and forth to the numeric keypad wastes seconds. For dedicated financial data entry involving columns of pure numbers, the 10-key keypad is faster.
faq.numbers.q3: What is the proper finger rule for the Shift key?
faq.numbers.a3: Always use the opposite hand's pinky to hold Shift. If you need to type a capital 'T' or the symbol '%', your right pinky holds the right Shift key while your left index finger strikes the key. Never press Shift and a letter using the same hand.
